questions.q: Does pre-heat cash reduce lost earnings and medical spending for outdoor-worker households?
questions.have: An urban heat protocol exists without a completed impact evaluation in the sources read. [N12]
questions.could: Randomised or pre-specified phased delivery across comparable neighbourhoods, recording timing, income, care and coping costs in aggregate.
questions.scale: Illustrative design: 40-60 clusters over two hot seasons; power calculation before final sampling.

questions.q: Which step limits qualifying SSF access among informal workers?
questions.have: Pre-launch awareness data and later registration reports describe different periods. [N7, N8]
questions.could: Follow a representative cohort from information through contribution qualification and benefit receipt, with anonymised aggregate reporting.
questions.scale: Illustrative design: 1,500-2,000 workers across several municipalities.

questions.q: How often does public insurance meet the full cost of heat-related care?
questions.have: Enrolment is measured; current heat-specific claims and complete costs are not. [N4, N5, N22]
questions.could: Prospective facility and household cost study with diagnosed heat cases, matched service records under consent, and published aggregate results only.
questions.scale: Illustrative design: 10-15 facilities across a hot season; case-volume check before sizing.

questions.q: Does a supported transfer process reduce allowance interruption after migration?
questions.have: A documented allowance transfer route exists; actual seasonal continuity was not measured. [N1]
questions.could: Phased assistance through wards, comparing aggregate transfer completion, payment interruption and travel cost.
questions.scale: Illustrative design: 20-30 ward pairs over one renewal and payment cycle.

evidence.title: Exploring outdoor workers’ knowledge, attitudes, practices, and perceived risks of heatwaves in Nepal
evidence.finding: KNOWN descriptive result: 43% had heard of heatwaves. This maps a communication gap among exposed workers; it does not estimate a social-protection effect.
evidence.limit: Selected locations, cross-sectional design and self-reported experiences limit generalisation and causality.

sources.label: Sharma et al., 2025: Exploring outdoor workers’ knowledge, attitudes, practices, and perceived risks of heatwaves in Nepal

evidence.title: Simplified Early Action Protocol: Nepal | Urban Heatwave
evidence.scale: Plan for 1,200 households and a three-day forecast lead time
evidence.finding: KNOWN approved plan: an urban heatwave protocol sets out cash and support activities. It supplies a possible route, with no completed impact result in the document read.
evidence.limit: Protocol approval is not activation, receipt, a standing public entitlement or an evaluation.

sources.label: International Federation of Red Cross and Red Crescent Societies / Nepal Red Cross Society, 2025: Simplified Early Action Protocol: Nepal | Urban Heatwave

evidence.title: Fast Action for Floods: RCT Evidence on Forecast-based Cash Transfers from Bangladesh and Nepal
evidence.scale: Randomised flood-related cash timing; country and survey-round samples differ
evidence.finding: KNOWN trial findings, with heat applicability INFERRED: some early food-security and psychosocial outcomes improved. Later borrowing, savings and asset effects were not statistically significant.
evidence.limit: Working paper and flood evidence; no statistically significant estimate does not establish zero effect, and it does not establish a heat effect.

sources.label: Christian et al., 2025: Fast Action for Floods: RCT Evidence on Forecast-based Cash Transfers from Bangladesh and Nepal

indicators.indicator: Days with daily maximum air temperature above 40 degrees C
indicators.definition: Proposed derivation from hourly ERA5 2 m temperature, using local calendar days and area-weighted aggregation. Threshold is an analytical choice, not an official warning threshold.
indicators.licence: CC-BY licence displayed; retain dataset attribution
indicators.place_code: Grid coordinates; spatial overlay with versioned province geometry
indicators.limit: INFERRED reanalysis; not measured personal exposure. No country values were calculated in this research.

indicators.indicator: Nights with daily minimum air temperature above 30 degrees C
indicators.definition: Proposed derivation from the same hourly series, using local-day minimum as a reproducible proxy. An overnight-only definition can be substituted if documented.
indicators.place_code: Same grid and geometry as hotdays
indicators.limit: INFERRED; a local-day minimum is not a direct measurement of sleep conditions.

indicators.definition: Proposed mean hourly 2 m dew-point temperature for March-June 2025, aggregated by area. This is a humidity context measure, not wet-bulb temperature or WBGT.
indicators.place_code: Same grid and geometry as hotdays
indicators.limit: INFERRED; a humid-heat health threshold has not been validated here. These variables are published on a grid, not as administrative tables.

indicators.definition: Proposed sum of five-year age groups from census Individual Table 04, divided by total population. This is a demographic measure, not an allowance eligibility threshold.
indicators.place_code: CSV code field not inspected; no shared code verified
indicators.limit: Catalogue is open, but CSV payload and smallest published unit were not parsed. Province aggregation is proposed, not a verified output. [N14]

indicators.limit: Catalogue confirms the table, not the header, geographic grain or benefit eligibility. [N14]
